region_scene_page.compact: The first mass rock and roll lane: R&B backbeat, country/blues forms, gospel charge, teen address, and short radio-ready records.
region_scene_page.standard: In the mid-1950s, Black R&B, gospel performance, blues structures, country boogie, independent labels, radio, jukeboxes, and TV converged into a new national youth sound. Chuck Berry, Little Richard, Fats Domino, Buddy Holly, Elvis Presley, and others made the language feel simple enough to dance to but strong enough to remake pop culture. It is compact, physical, and direct: the song hits quickly, the rhythm is blunt, the singer sounds like an event, and the guitar or piano usually gives the record its signature shape.
